claim: A cold normal Omarchy boot on Pixel 6 is usable as a mobile Agent node with responsive GPU rendering, Wi-Fi recovery, China Mobile data and at least the supported cameras.
oracle: The user can boot to the graphical desktop, open and type in an Agent terminal without a first-launch stall, join authorized Wi-Fi and resume after one link drop, register the inserted China Mobile SIM with a 4G or 5G bearer and complete one HTTPS Agent request, and capture a frame from the supported front or ultra-wide camera.

user_journey.scenario: From a cold boot away from the laptop, the user touches the desktop, opens an Agent terminal, joins Wi-Fi, briefly loses coverage, then checks mobile data and camera access.
user_journey.expected: The desktop stays responsive, the Agent request either succeeds or reports a specific layer failure, Wi-Fi reconnects without losing USB recovery, mobile registration is visible without exposing identifiers, and camera preview/capture works for a supported sensor.

invariants: Slot A Android remains the recovery path; hardware trials write only approved slot-B images and userdata through the project tools.
No public artifact contains firmware, calibration, IMEI, serial number, MAC address, SSID or credentials.
GPU, Wi-Fi, cellular and camera are enabled one at a time with a watchdog and serial log before the next gate.
The main GN1 camera remains excluded until its CSIS frame errors are fixed; front IMX355 and ultra-wide IMX386 are the initial camera oracle.
Cellular data is not inferred from a cdc-wdm node: registration, bearer, route and HTTPS are all required.
gitnexus: The public device package stages read-only probes and inactive optional profiles; no profile is enabled by an unrelated boot path.
The GS101 source checker and preparation script are the only public kernel source boundary; firmware and modem NV remain outside the repository.
ast: The hardware snapshot separates render nodes, devfreq, CPU rate limits, network interfaces, cellular control nodes and camera nodes.
The Agent probe independently checks IPv4, DNS and HTTPS, so an interface node cannot be mistaken for usable service traffic.

unit.red: Offline fixtures intentionally fail when a route, renderer, camera node or cellular control node is absent.
unit.green: Network, snapshot, optional-profile and apply/rollback fixtures pass; kernel and libcamera contracts must pass in their own source trees.
cases: no GPU render node or software renderer
missing Wi-Fi interface, route, DNS or HTTPS
cellular control node without registered bearer
optional profile rollback after an interrupted change

boundaries: GS101 kernel and private firmware -> systemd/Hyprland -> touch and GPU
S5123 CPIF -> ModemManager/NetworkManager -> China Mobile bearer
GS101 CSIS and IMX355/IMX386 -> libcamera -> preview/capture
evidence: Existing diagnostic evidence proves GPU first draw on two boots and Wi-Fi association/reconnect; the cold normal desktop, cellular and camera gates remain open.

limitations: A source build or device-node snapshot cannot prove physical smoothness, SIM registration or camera frames.
The current public tree does not redistribute Google's firmware or the modem's per-phone NV data.
The main rear GN1 sensor remains unsupported in the reference path.
exit_gate: All four user-visible journeys pass on the same cold boot series, with a fresh serial recovery check after each fault and redacted evidence recorded in a new release manifest.
